rationale: Although situated in the general field of rural community water supply, this article describes a 1998 training workshop organized to establish Information Focal Points (IFPs) within four partner NGOs/research centres to disseminate research results. It fails Criterion 2 (E03: research dissemination and documentation initiative rather than a legal or administrative mechanism governing water access), Criterion 3 (descriptive workshop report providing organizational thumbnail sketches and implementation plans rather than an empirical study or systematic review), and Criterion 4 (no household or community water access outcome).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings: the article reports on a research-dissemination training workshop to set up organizational Information Focal Points rather than examining any legal, administrative, regulatory, or governance factor shaping water service access, and it also lacks empirical primary evidence or service-access outcomes.

evidence_quotes.quote: Development of Information Focal Points (IFPs) on Community Water Supply in Rural Areas: An Initiative to Disseminate Research Results

At the end of 1998 a training workshop was organized by the IRC International Water and Sanitation Centre in The Hague, The Netherlands, with the aim of establishing Information Focal Points (IFPs) within a number of organizations.
This article describes the objectives and outcomes of the above workshop and provides thumbnail sketches of the partner organizations involved in the sub-project.
